clue.text: A costing process he claims not to know

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An accountant's costing procedure that its author admits he does not understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' is the anagram signal: A COSTING rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of this belief holds that the existence of God cannot be known, so he professes ignorance.

clue.text: Bill sees programmed note retrieved from computer

parts.note: ACC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: programmed means arranged to a set plan, so the letters of sees are rearranged

parts.note: D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone checks an invoice after a computer has printed a reminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programmed' rearranges SEES into ESSE, which sits between ACC (account) and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Data that has been fetched from a computer's storage has been looked up and opened there.

clue.text: Keep going on about how to use an embrocation

explanation.surface: Advice on applying a liniment, framed as nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to harp on someone's mistake; literally, a liniment is massaged into the skin.

clue.text: A group of investigators put in charge is sharp

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A team of detectives given command of a case proves keen.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour or biting taste or remark is described this way, like vinegar.

clue.text: Working habits provoking ridicule in Nazi security forces

indicators.note: the ridicule word is placed inside the abbreviation for the Nazi forces

parts.note: SS, the Schutzstaffel, were Nazi security forces
to mock is to ridicule

explanation.surface: Nazi guards provoke laughter with their clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' are garments here, not routines: loose overalls worn for work.
explanation.definitionFit: These loose overgarments are worn to protect clothes while working, and a habit is a garment.

clue.text: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?

definitions.text: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?

parts.words: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?
parts.note: the Lords Spiritual are bishops in the House of Lords; one favouring traditional, ceremonial Anglican worship is the person meant

explanation.surface: A bishop in the House of Lords who leans to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' suggests party politics, but here it means traditional, ritual-loving Anglicanism.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican favouring elaborate ritual and Catholic tradition holds a conservative churchmanship.

clue.text: Two former Prime Ministers possess the right to symbolise the house

indicators.note: the Prime Ministers hold the letter for right inside them

parts.note: Edward Heath and Alec Douglas-Home were both British Prime Ministers
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Two ex-premiers claim the right to stand for the British household.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATH and HOME were British Prime Ministers of the 1960s and 70s; R goes inside HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside and dwelling together are a stock phrase standing for domestic life.

clue.text: Preservation society which has the confidence of the people

parts.note: something belonging to a whole people or country is national
confidence in someone is trust

explanation.surface: A heritage charity is trusted by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The British charity that conserves historic buildings and landscapes.

clue.text: Transatlantic girl with mineral wealth in abundance

parts.note: gal is an American word for a girl
ore is mined rock rich in metal

explanation.surface: An American woman has plenty of mining riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means aplenty and follows its noun, as in 'prizes aplenty'.

clue.text: Show I acted in by order

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them differently, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor says he was cast in a production on instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by order' signals that I ACTED IN is to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out or signal something is to show it.

clue.text: Conventional group of people

explanation.surface: A description of a conformist crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed and established, as in set ways; also a clique, as in the smart set.

clue.text: Conditions in North America

explanation.surface: Circumstances in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Situations or circumstances; also the informal name for the USA, the United States of North America.

clue.text: In the Channel Islands senate initially gets no one to back cut

parts.note: taken as written
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of senate
going back means the words for no and one are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Channel Islands' parliament fails to find a single supporter for a spending cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses NO + I to give ION after IN, CI and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's slit into tissue is a cut.

clue.text: Heiress whose heart is filled with anger

indicators.note: the central letters of heiress contain the answer, sitting in its heart

explanation.surface: A rich heiress is furious inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for wrath or fury.

clue.text: Downfall of a rotter in a legal action

indicators.note: the rotter is placed inside the legal action

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel brought down by a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' is not ruin but a fall of water, like a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall tumbling down in stages is a fall of water, a downfall.

clue.text: A measurement of twelve inches at the stern

parts.note: FT abbreviates foot, which is twelve inches

explanation.surface: A precise measurement taken at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically, towards or at the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Hard cheese! It's in the Mendips

explanation.surface: Bad luck, says someone about a Somerset place.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm cheese; also a village with a famous gorge in the Mendip Hills of Somerset, England.

clue.text: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!

definitions.text: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!

parts.words: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!
parts.note: pushy salesmanship pressures customers into purchase; read literally, the name says the goods are difficult to shift

explanation.surface: Pushy salesmen make buying effortless.
explanation.walkthrough: The name literally says selling is difficult, while the technique makes buying easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful, high-pressure salesmanship is the opposite of the soft sell.

clue.text: Remove from the House of Hades

parts.note: Dis is a name for Hades, the Roman god of the underworld
a lodge is a house, often a small one

explanation.surface: Someone is driven out of the underworld's palace.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something out of its place is to remove it.

clue.text: Divided as to where Tom Sawyer might be found

definitions.text: where Tom Sawyer might be found

explanation.surface: A boy's adventures split between pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for into two parts; Tom Sawyer appears in the novels of Mark Twain.

clue.text: Taking on a child is a choice of the present era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Adopting a child is a modern option.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally taking another's child as one's own.

clue.text: He carries cases of wine with little hesitation

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
er is the sound of a brief hesitation

explanation.surface: A man hesitantly carries crates of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests wine crates but means luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or hotel employee carries luggage.

clue.text: I get Sid to throw out imbeciles

indicators.note: throwing letters out of their order scrambles them

explanation.surface: Someone gets Sid to expel fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Fools and dimwits.

clue.text: Following breakdown sister takes the examination again

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the word apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sister retakes her exam after a nervous breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Students who failed sit the test a second time.

clue.text: Make hay, Edward

explanation.surface: An instruction to a farmhand named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread grass for drying; also a short form of Edward.

clue.text: Not a good outlook in the opinion of theneedy

explanation.surface: The poor take a dim view of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfavourable prospect or attitude; literally the poor's view, the outlook of those without money.

clue.text: Plug recommendation to defer retirement

explanation.surface: Advice to keep working beyond pension age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' means going to bed: the advice is to stay awake late.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a hole; also an instruction to stay awake rather than go to bed.

clue.text: If you've got it you're not in the dark

definitions.text: If you've got it you're not in the dark

parts.words: If you've got it you're not in the dark
parts.note: the reading suggests understanding, but literally it is domestic illumination from the mains

explanation.surface: Understanding something means you are well informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the dark' suggests ignorance, but literally it means without illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumination from a bulb powered by the mains keeps a room from darkness.
